social_security.summary: California does not adopt the federal rule that taxes Social Security, so U.S. Social Security and Tier 1 Railroad Retirement benefits are excluded from California income.

sources.quote: (a) Section 86 of the Internal Revenue Code, relating to Social Security and Tier 1 Railroad Retirement Benefits, shall not apply.
Line 6 – Social Security Benefits California excludes U.S. social security benefits or equivalent Tier 1 railroad retirement benefits from taxable income.

public_pension.summary: California has no special exclusion for state, local or federal government pensions; a resident's pension is taxed like other income, generally in the same amount as federally.

sources.quote: Part II of Subchapter B of Chapter 1 of Subtitle A of the Internal Revenue Code, relating to items that are specifically included in gross income, shall apply, except as otherwise provided.
Line 5a and Line 5b – Pensions and Annuities Generally, no adjustments are made on this line.

private_pension.summary: Private pensions, 401(k) and IRA distributions are taxed by California like other income, generally in the same amount as federally.

sources.quote: Section 61 of the Internal Revenue Code, relating to gross income defined, shall apply, except as otherwise provided.
Line 4a and Line 4b – IRA Distributions Generally, no adjustments are made on this line.
Line 5a and Line 5b – Pensions and Annuities Generally, no adjustments are made on this line.

military_retirement.summary: For tax years 2025 through 2029, a qualified taxpayer may exclude up to $20,000 of U.S. uniformed services retired pay; the exclusion is limited to taxpayers with federal AGI up to $125,000 ($250,000 joint or surviving spouse), and the rest is taxable.
conditions: Up to $20,000 of uniformed services retirement pay excluded
Federal AGI not over $125,000 (single/other) or $250,000 (joint or surviving spouse)
A separate $20,000 exclusion applies to DoD Survivor Benefit Plan annuities

sources.quote: (a) For taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025, and before January 1, 2030, gross income shall not include retirement pay received by a qualified taxpayer during the taxable year, not to exceed twenty thousand dollars ($20,000), from the federal government for service in the uniformed services.

For taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025, and before January 1, 2030, California allows qualified taxpayers to exclude from gross income up to $20,000 of retirement pay from the federal government for service in the uniformed services
In the case of an individual, the taxpayer’s income may not exceed $125,000.

notes: The military retirement exclusion (R&TC 17132.9, plus 17132.10 for Survivor Benefit Plan annuities) is new for tax year 2025 and sunsets after tax year 2029; it is an income-limited exclusion, so retirees above the AGI limits are fully taxed. FTB has published analyses of 2026 bills that would raise or remove the $20,000 cap; whether any was enacted was not checked, and the index text quoted is the $20,000 version. California taxes residents on pensions from any state; nonresidents are not taxed on qualified retirement income (federal law, 4 U.S.C. 114).
